The bridge E edges out the hub C, 0.159 to 0.156, ahead of D 0.147, while the pendant G, behind a single edge, scores 0.070." width="100%"} Closeness centrality uses shortest-path distances; current-flow closeness uses *effective resistance* instead, treating each edge as a resistor (Brandes & Fleischer 2005). The effective resistance between two nodes is small when they are joined by many short, parallel routes, so it accounts for every path rather than only the shortest. The score is the reciprocal of a node's total effective resistance to all others. It is the same measure as Stephenson & Zelen's *information centrality*, which NetworkX also exposes as `information_centrality()`. Edge weights act as conductances (higher weight, lower resistance). The graph must be undirected and connected. For the resistances themselves, see `resistance_distance_matrix()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights as conductances. If `None` (default), follows the graph. Weights must be positive. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to store scores in. If `None` (default), uses `"current_flow_closeness_centrality"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the scores as a node attribute and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: a dictionary mapping node IDs to scores. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed or disconnected, or a weight is not positive. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~closeness_centrality`) : Count shortest paths only. [](`~current_flow_betweenness_centrality`) : How much current passes through each node. ## Examples {.doc-examples} The hub of a star is electrically closest to everyone: ::: {#346c98b7 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec star = ec.Graph().add_star_graph(n=5) star.current_flow_closeness_centrality().get_node_df().select( "label", "current_flow_closeness_centrality" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ### Many routes, or a short one Current-flow closeness measures distance by electrical resistance, which falls with every extra route between two nodes. In Zachary's karate club, the administrator (member 33) ranks first by it, though third by closeness. Member 19, eighth by closeness because its three friends include both leaders, is only fifteenth, since three ties make few routes: ::: {#5da4337e .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl club = ( ec.karate_club() .layout_kamada_kawai() .current_flow_closeness_centrality() .closeness_centrality() ) ( club.get_node_df() .with_columns( pl.col("current_flow_closeness_centrality", "closeness_centrality") .rank("min", descending=True) .name.suffix("_rank") ) .filter(pl.col("label").is_in(["0", "33", "19"])) .select( "label", "current_flow_closeness_centrality_rank", "closeness_centrality_rank", ) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Edge weights act as conductances, so pass `weighted=False` when they measure a distance or a cost.
